entries.title: Job 7:1
segments:
An appointed time; or, a warfare. 
 
  He means that his whole life is, as it were, a warfare. 
 
  Like the days of a hireling; occupied with hard labor, so that he longs for their close,
The length of human life is fixed by God; and all the days of our appointed time we should wait with patience, and labor with diligence, till our change come.

entries.title: Job 7:3
segments: Months of vanity--wearisome nights; so that, like the hireling, I long to have the day of life close.

entries.title: Job 7:5
segments: No perfection of human character will exempt men in this world from trials; and none but those who have experienced them, can realize the difficulty of exercising at all times a calm, quiet, peaceful submission under them.

entries.title: Job 7:6
segments: Without hope; of recovery, or any relief except in death.

entries.title: Job 7:8
segments: Are upon me--am not; or, "shall be upon me, and I shall not be." Thou shalt seek me, but I shall no more be found in the land of the living,

entries.title: Job 7:12
segments: Thou settest a watch over me; guardest me as if I needed strong restraint.

entries.title: Job 7:13
segments: Quiet and refreshing rest in sleep is the gift of God, and a blessing the greatness of which no one who has not for a time been deprived of it will duly appreciate.

entries.title: Job 7:16
segments: Let me alone; cease from troubling me during the brief day of life.

entries.title: Job 7:17
segments: Magnify him; make so much account of him in the way of chastisement and discipline.

entries.title: Job 7:19
segments: Till I swallow down my spittle; a proverbial expression, meaning, till I have a little respite.

entries.title: Job 7:20
segments:
Set me as a mark; for the arrows of the Almighty. 
 
All men have sinned, and deserve all that they suffer; and the only sure way of deliverance is in acknowledging their transgressions, and looking up to Him who is exalted to give repentance, that he would freely and abundantly pardon.

entries.title: Job 7:21
segments: For now shall I sleep in the dust; he means, that if God does not soon pardon his transgression, and restore to him the light of his countenance, there will be no more opportunity to show him kindness, since he is passing down rapidly to the grave.
